name: Tahiti
description: Tahiti is an alternative name for Big Two (also known as Cho Dai Di, Big Deuce, and Top Dog). It is a popular climbing card game of Chinese origin where players try to be the first to get rid of all their cards by playing singles or combinations (pairs, triples, poker hands) that beat the previous play. The Two is the highest rank.
origin: China (often called Tahiti in Western circles)

history.origins: Originating in coastal China (likely Shanghai) around 1980, the game spread globally. The name 'Tahiti' is one of several Western monikers for Big Two.
timeline: 1980s: Game emerged in coastal China (Shanghai); spread globally under the name Tahiti in Western circles.
history.cultural: A staple in East Asian communities and widely played socially and for stakes.
history.evolution: See Big Two for detailed evolution.

setup.dealing: Deal the entire deck (13 cards to each of 4 players).

rules.objective: The object of the game is to be the first to get rid of all of your cards, by playing them to the table. Cards can be played singly or in certain combinations. If you cannot be first to play all your cards, then your aim is to have as few cards as possible when another player finishes.
rules.gameplay: Player with 3 of Diamonds starts. Play moves clockwise. Players must beat the previous play with a higher card or combination of the same type (Single, Pair, Triple, 5-card Poker Hand). 2 is high. Suit order usually applies (Diamonds < Clubs < Hearts < Spades). Pass if you cannot or do not wish to play. A new round starts when all pass.
keyRules: Must beat previous play with same number of cards (except in some variants)
Suit order matters for breaking ties

strategy.basic: Gain control of the lead to play your weak small cards. Save 2s to win control back.
strategy.intermediate: Count cards (especially 2s and Aces). Break up hands only when necessary to win a round.
strategy.advanced: Trap opponents with high cards. Calculate if you can go out in one turn (run the deck).
tips: Don't waste a 2 on a small single if you can win with an Ace.
Watch out for players with few cards left.
